findings.description: Critical: the envelope's own identity validator is never named in the widening set, and its non-operation branch rejects every system_check alert at construction. Task 3.7 widens five elements (source kind, event-key grammar, workflow type, diagnostic-URL validator, diagnostic codes), and D5's table pins 'event_key grammar' to workflow_alert_models.py:141-176 -- that range is WorkflowTerminalEventV1.validate_source_identity (:152), a different class from the envelope. WorkflowAlertEnvelopeV1._validate_identity_and_collections (:296) is cited nowhere in design.md, tasks.md, or the amendments. Its else-branch (:322-323) raises 'reconciliation alerts must omit operation_id and use workflow type' unless workflow_type == 'content.reconciliation', then requires attempt == 1 and an event_key matching one of two reconciliation regexes. A system_check envelope carrying workflow_type 'system.backup_freshness' hits that branch and raises before any of the five widened elements matter. This is the same failure mode A2 corrected for the key grammar -- rejected at construction, so no alert is ever emitted -- surviving in a second location.
findings.resolution: Add _validate_identity_and_collections (workflow_alert_models.py:296-340) to D5's widening table and to task 3.7's element list as a third source_kind branch: for system_check, require operation_id/attempt absent, workflow_type == 'system.backup_freshness', event_key matching the A2 grammar, and diagnostic_url path == /api/v1/workflow-terminal-events/{event_id}. Have task 3.6 assert construction of a system_check envelope succeeds, so the gap fails a test rather than surfacing at integration.

findings.description: Critical: the alert JSON Schema omits four fields that WorkflowAlertEnvelopeV1 makes mandatory, and types a fifth as null where the model requires a positive int. The model declares attempt: Annotated[int, Field(ge=1, ...)] (:232) -- non-nullable and required -- plus resource_refs (:234), source_keys (:238) and counts (:239), none with defaults. The schema's required list is [schema_version, event_id, event_key, occurred_at, severity, outcome, source_kind, workflow_type, diagnostic_url, codes] and it declares attempt as {'type': 'null'}. A payload that satisfies the schema therefore fails model construction on four missing fields, and any payload the model accepts carries an attempt the schema forbids. D5 says operation_id and attempt must 'be made optional for the new kind', but task 3.7's element list does not include attempt, so the nullability change has no owning task. Task 3.7b's conformance assertion ('the event schema landed in 0.2 agrees with WorkflowAlertEnvelopeV1') fails by construction against the schema as written.
findings.resolution: Regenerate contracts/events/backup-freshness-alert.schema.json against the widened model: add resource_refs, source_keys and counts to required (empty list / empty object are the system_check values), and make attempt's schema type match whatever task 3.7 changes the model field to. Add attempt nullability explicitly to task 3.7's element list and to D5's table so it has an owner.

findings.description: Critical: the alert schema declares two properties that do not exist on WorkflowAlertEnvelopeV1, and StrictModel forbids extras. The schema defines claim_generation and terminal_status (both 'type': 'null') with descriptions calling them 'absent for system checks'. Those fields exist on WorkflowTerminalEventV1 (:145-147), not on the envelope, whose field list ends at codes (:240). StrictModel sets model_config = ConfigDict(extra='forbid') (workflow_models.py:69-70), so an envelope payload carrying either key raises a validation error rather than ignoring it. Because the schema also omits additionalProperties: false, it is simultaneously more permissive than the model everywhere else -- it will not catch a genuinely misspelled field.
findings.resolution: Drop claim_generation and terminal_status from the alert schema -- the envelope has no such fields, so the null-typed declarations describe a shape that can never validate. Set additionalProperties: false to mirror extra='forbid'. Both are properties of the schema-vs-model conformance test in task 3.7b; state them there so the test is written to assert field-set equality, not just field-by-field compatibility.

findings.description: Critical: the diagnostic_url pattern admits http://, which the model rejects and no producer emits. The schema pins diagnostic_url to '^https?://[^/]+/api/v1/workflow-terminal-events/<uuid>$'. The model field is WorkflowDiagnosticUrl = Annotated[AnyUrl, UrlConstraints(max_length=2048, allowed_schemes=['https'])] (:133-136) -- https only -- and the sole producer hardcodes the scheme: workflow_terminal_event_service.py:568 builds origin = f'https://{parsed.netloc}'. So the optional 's' describes a URL that is unreachable from the code and rejected at the boundary. A6 exists to close silent-success gaps; this is the inverse, a contract looser than the thing it documents, and it is exactly what task 3.7b's conformance test is meant to catch.
findings.resolution: Change the pattern to require https:// literally, matching UrlConstraints(allowed_schemes=['https']).

findings.description: Critical: A2's event-key grammar contradicts D6's idempotency rationale, and D6 was not amended. D6 states under a bolded 'Definition of "check window"' that idempotency is 'keyed, not timed by wall clock', deriving the key from the observed manifest generation ('system_check:backup_stale:<manifest_completed_at>', with a UTC date for no_history) and drawing the consequence that 'while a backup stays stale the manifest timestamp does not move, so exactly one alert exists no matter how often maintenance runs'. A2 replaces this with 'system_check:backup_freshness:<epoch-seconds>' where the suffix is 'the check-window start' -- a wall-clock quantity -- and asserts 'idempotency-per-window is preserved'. Under A2 a persistently stale backup emits a new alert every window, which is the alert storm D6 was written to prevent; under D6 it emits one. A2's header says it supersedes 'D5's key sketch' only, so D6's text stands as normative and the two conflict. Compounding this, no artifact defines the window's duration: design.md:165/168, tasks.md:206 and spec.md:290/309 all say 'per check window' without ever fixing its length, so the alert volume for a sustained outage is unspecified.
findings.resolution: Amend D6 explicitly rather than leaving it standing, and state the window duration as a number in one place (the spec requirement is the right home, since tasks.md:206 tests against it). Then state the intended behaviour for a sustained stale condition -- one alert total, or one per window -- and make task 3.8's 'one alert per check window' assertion test that decision.

findings.description: Nit: the diagnostic-code set still disagrees across three artifacts, and the gap widened rather than closed. Round-1 finding 15 flagged the alert schema listing four codes against D5's three. The schema now enumerates six -- backup_stale, backup_no_history, backup_partial, backup_verify_failed, backup_target_unreachable, backup_environment_mismatch -- while D5's widening table still reads 'add backup_stale, backup_no_history, backup_verify_failed'. A6 introduced backup_partial and backup_environment_mismatch without updating D5's table, and backup_target_unreachable appears in no design text at all. Task 3.7 says only 'diagnostic codes' without enumerating, so nothing reconciles them; WorkflowAlertDiagnosticCode is a closed Literal union, so any code missed at implementation raises at construction.
findings.resolution: Update D5's table to the full six-code set, or replace the enumeration with a pointer to the schema as the single source of truth. Either way, name the schema as authoritative in task 3.7 so the implementer widens the Literal union from one list.

findings.description: Nit: wp-contracts still locks the alert schema at a path it will never write. Round-1 finding 14 was half-applied: scope.write_allow gained openspec/contracts/content-workflows/events/**, matching contracts/README.md:22 ('the alert schema lands in content-workflows, not in the new backup domain'), but locks.files still names openspec/contracts/backup/events/backup-freshness-alert.schema.json. The lock therefore guards an unwritten path while the real target is unguarded -- harmless for a single-package run, but the lock is the coordination boundary the package description leans on ('Runs first so downstream packages code against a fixed shape').
findings.resolution: Change wp-contracts locks.files to openspec/contracts/content-workflows/events/backup-freshness-alert.schema.json so lock and write scope name the same object.

findings.description: Nit: A6 made the shared-bucket collision loud but left the collision itself, and the cheap structural fix was not taken. spec.md:19 still has backup_s3_prefix default to the shared constant 'aca', and spec.md:202 still requires the manifest at 'a stable, well-known key under the configured prefix'. Two environments on one bucket at the default prefix therefore still write the same object. A6's environment field converts the old silent failure (staging's fresh timestamp masking a dead production backup) into a detected one, which is the important half. What remains is that both environments then sit permanently in environment-mismatch: each run clobbers the other's manifest, so neither has a usable freshness signal and both alert continuously. Backup artifacts are unaffected -- they live under tier and timestamp keys -- so this costs monitoring, not recoverability.
findings.resolution: Require the manifest key to carry the environment segment (e.g. <prefix>/manifest/<environment>/latest.json) so the two environments cannot address the same object. The environment field and its rejection rule stay as the defence for a misconfigured prefix.

findings.description: Nit: the schema's UUID pattern is looser than the validator it documents, in two ways. diagnostic_url matches '[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}', which constrains neither the version nor the variant nibble, while _is_canonical_uuid (:436-441) requires parsed.version in {1,2,3,4,5} and str(parsed) == value. A UUIDv7 diagnostic URL -- a plausible choice for a new emitter -- validates against the schema and is rejected by the model. Separately, the model's non-operation branch requires path == f'/api/v1/workflow-terminal-events/{self.event_id}' (:325-327), tying the URL's UUID to the envelope's own event_id; the schema accepts any UUID in that position, so a payload whose diagnostic_url points at a different event validates.
findings.resolution: Tighten the version/variant nibbles in the pattern to match _is_canonical_uuid. The event_id correspondence is not expressible in JSON Schema -- record it as an assertion in task 3.7b's conformance test instead of trying to encode it.

findings.description: Optional: backup_staleness_hours keeps the legacy 48-hour default (spec.md:58, 'SHALL default to the same value as the legacy staleness setting it replaces') against a daily schedule and D2's stated 24-hour RPO, so two consecutive failed runs elapse before anything is reported. Round-1 finding 23 raised this and the plan kept parity. The choice is defensible -- parity is what makes the railway_backup_staleness_hours forward-mapping in specs/database-provider/spec.md:29 a true no-op rename, and changing the default silently retunes existing deployments -- so this is flagged as a conscious trade-off rather than a defect.
findings.resolution: Either accept and note in D2 that the alerting threshold is deliberately 2x the RPO, or set the new setting's default to 24 and treat the changed threshold as a documented behavioural change in the deprecation mapping.

findings.description: The round-1 criticals were propagated into the downstream artifacts, not just appended as prose to design.md -- which is the usual failure mode for an amendment round. Spot-verified: the 'no migration' claim is retracted in proposal.md:159-173 rather than quietly edited; A1's migration has real tasks (3.7c-3.7g, including an alembic heads check) and wp-health-alerts' write scope actually gained alembic/versions/**, src/queue/setup.py, src/models/workflow_alert.py and src/services/workflow_terminal_event_service.py; A8's ownership move is reflected in work-packages.yaml as a wp-health-alerts -> wp-backup-cli dependency with the deny list narrowed to src/services/backup/manifest_reader.py; A4's (graphdb_provider, graphdb_mode) branch and A5's write-time retention tiers appear as spec scenarios (spec.md:89-105, :81-86).

A6's four silent-success defences landed as observable spec scenarios rather than design prose, which is what makes them testable: per-stage exit status with an explicit prohibition on trusting the final stage (spec.md:134-139), a size read-back against the stored object (:144), the run path preflighting its binaries (:154) rather than leaving that on verify where D13 never wires it to the timer, and fresh-but-partial explicitly not reporting healthy (:234-238). A7's decision to tee into sha256sum inside the same pipeline is the right call for a change whose core property is that multi-GB dumps never enter the interpreter.
